FIFO EXCEPTION ON THE MERGE QUEUE, AUTHORIZED BY NATHAN, 2026-08-19. Recording it BEFORE it happens rather than explaining it afterwards, because a queue whose order can be departed from silently is not a queue.

WHAT: req-3163ceb2c101 (fix/probe-tier-and-lean-merge, arrived 19:20:49) runs ahead of three rows that arrived first — campaign/the-crucible 17:49:39, campaign/the-burr 18:49:29, fix/census-yellow-teeth 18:52:28.

WHY, with the arithmetic that motivated it. Mean phase wall time measured across today's chamber runs on this box:

  heavy       1965.0 s (21 runs)     gate        342.6 s (32 runs)
  seam-guard  1017.5 s (21 runs)     clients     248.6 s (26 runs)
                                     artifacts    99.4 s (34 runs)
                                     outboard     30.6 s (34 runs)

Six phases ~3704 s (62 min); four ~721 s (12 min). The candidate removes seam-guard and heavy from merges (decision 0148), i.e. 80.5% of a merge's wall time. Running it first makes the three rows it jumps cost ~36 min in total instead of ~3 h.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not a priority tier. Decision 0133 says first-come-first-served, no priority tiers, no force override, and that stands — one authorized exception by the decider is not a tier, and the next operator should NOT read this as licence to reorder on a cost argument of their own. I declined to do exactly that twice today, once for the fix that was unblocking a held campaign of mine; the difference here is that Nathan asked, not that the arithmetic got better.

WHAT IT COSTS THE JUMPED ROWS: about twelve minutes each of additional wait, since the jumping candidate is itself a four-phase-sized job under the old six-phase rule. They then run ~50 min cheaper each. Both campaigns have been told directly.

THE THING THAT WOULD MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY NEXT TIME: nothing in the queue can express "this job makes every subsequent job cheaper". That is a real gap and not one I am fixing under an exception — noting it here so a future campaign can decide whether the queue wants a notion of an infrastructure candidate at all, or whether one-off authorization is the honest mechanism precisely because it forces a human to look.
